steps.say: We can put chance on a scale from impossible to certain.
steps.show: impossible, unlikely, even chance, likely, certain

steps.say: Even chance means it is just as likely to happen as not to happen.

figure.alt: A spinner with 2 equal parts, 1 part shaded.

steps.say: A coin landing on heads is an even chance. It lands on heads or tails.
6 out of 8 parts are shaded, so landing on a shaded part is likely.

figure.alt: A spinner with 8 equal parts, 6 parts shaded.

steps.say: A dice has 6 numbers. Rolling an even number is an even chance.

check.prompt: A bag has 4 red counters and 4 blue counters. How likely is picking red?

options.why: There are not more red counters than blue ones.
There are not fewer red counters than blue ones.
Some counters are blue, so red is not certain.

hints: Count the red counters and the blue counters.
Are there more of one colour?
check.explanation: There are 4 red and 4 blue counters, the same number of each. So picking red is an even chance.

check.prompt: A normal dice is rolled. Which is most likely?

options.why: A normal dice has no 7, so it is impossible.

hints: List the dice numbers that make each one happen.
More numbers that work means more likely.
check.explanation: A number less than 5 works for 4 numbers out of 6. That is more than any of the others.
